articles.title: An Eclipse Over Zambia
articles.summary: This article recounts an expedition to Lusaka, Zambia, for the total solar eclipse on June 21, 2001, where a group of "migrant travelers" observed the celestial event, witnessing a "triple diamond ring" and an unexpected marriage proposal. Beyond the eclipse, the narrative details extensive travels through Africa, including visits to Victoria Falls, the Hwange Game Preserve, and the Great Zimbabwe Ruins, alongside observations of the Southern night sky. The author also shares technical details about eclipse photography techniques and their overall 12-day adventure.

articles.title: Birdwatching at the Grand Canyon
articles.summary: This article recounts the author's experience at the 2001 Grand Canyon Star Party, blending terrestrial birdwatching with celestial observations of constellations named after birds. While observing the Milky Way and constellations like Cygnus, Aquila, and Corvus, the author also focuses on the remarkable California Condor, highlighting its history, conservation status, and majestic presence at the Grand Canyon. The narrative intertwines detailed descriptions of astronomical objects with the awe of observing an endangered bird in its natural habitat.

articles.title: Lessons From Polyphemus
articles.summary: Andrew Pierce recounts his experience borrowing a 14.5-inch Dobsonian telescope from the SJAA loaner program, exploring the challenges and rewards of using a large-aperture instrument. He details his journey to become a "Big Dob Guy," from navigating to star parties and learning to assemble and collimate the scope, to ultimately appreciating the deep-sky views it provided, even highlighting its unexpected capabilities in suburban settings. The article reflects on the trade-offs between aperture and portability, offering practical lessons for aspiring large-scope owners.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article details a trip to Hawaii's Big Island, comparing its diverse volcanic landscapes to the Moon and Mars. The author explores how Hawaii's geologically young formations, such as collapsing lava tubes and shield volcanoes, offer insights into the early geology of other celestial bodies. A true 'moonscape' was found atop Mauna Kea, providing an Earth-based simulation of lunar and Martian terrains.

articles.title: A Daytime Occultation of Jupiter
articles.summary: This article details astronomical observing opportunities for August, emphasizing the diminishing but still discernible features of Mars in early August and the return of Saturn. The primary event highlighted is a daytime occultation of Jupiter by a thin crescent Moon on August 15, providing specific timings and practical observation tips, including safety precautions.

articles.title: Around The Galaxy
articles.summary: This article reviews "Around The Galaxy," an excellent 37-part BBC-produced series on the Discovery/Science Channel that covers astronomy topics from creation to black holes and future space exploration. Author Tom Zeglin highly recommends the educational series, featuring top scientists and animations, and is taping all episodes. Zeglin offers to make the recorded series available for community members to check out.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article details the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) telescope loaner program, providing comprehensive lists of scopes currently available, those recently loaned out, and those with extended loan periods. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop for borrowing information, to be placed on a waiting list, or to inquire about a scope on extended loan. The document also includes an update on a recently donated telescope undergoing repairs before becoming available.
